Capital Budgeting: NPV, IRR, Payback and Profitability Index

Capital budgeting is how a company decides which long-term projects to invest in. This guide applies every major method to one project, and shows why NPV is usually preferred.

2 min readFor MBA, BBA and BBMUpdated 2 November 2026

The example project

A machine costs ₹10,00,000 today. It should bring in cash of ₹3,00,000, ₹3,50,000, ₹4,00,000, ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000 over five years. The required return is 12%.

YearCash flow (₹)Present value at 12% (₹)Cumulative PV (₹)
13,00,0002,67,8572,67,857
23,50,0002,79,0185,46,875
34,00,0002,84,7128,31,587

The methods and their results

MethodHow it worksResultDecision rule

How the payback is worked out

After 2 years, ₹6,50,000 has come back, leaving ₹3,50,000. Year 3 brings ₹4,00,000, so that takes 3,50,000 ÷ 4,00,000 = 0.875 of the year. Payback is 2.875 years, or about 2.88. Simple payback ignores both the time value of money and everything after the payback date.

Why NPV is usually preferred

  • It measures the wealth added in rupees, which is the goal of the firm.
  • It uses every cash flow and allows for the time value of money.
  • NPVs of separate projects can be added together.
  • IRR can mislead: projects with unusual cash flows can have several IRRs, and IRR assumes reinvestment at the IRR itself.

NPV and IRR can disagree

For a single project, they give the same accept-or-reject answer. For mutually exclusive projects of different sizes or timing, they can rank them differently: a small project may have a higher IRR but a lower NPV. In that case, choose the higher NPV, as it adds more value. Modified IRR (MIRR) fixes the reinvestment problem by assuming reinvestment at the cost of capital.

Which cash flows count

  • Use incremental cash flows, meaning only those caused by the project.
  • Ignore sunk costs already spent, such as last year's consultancy fee.
  • Include opportunity costs, such as the rent you lose by using your own building.
  • Exclude interest, because the discount rate already covers the cost of finance.
  • Include changes in working capital and the final salvage value.

Exam and interview questions

What is the discount rate in NPV?

Usually the project's required return, based on the firm's cost of capital (WACC) adjusted for the risk of the project.

Why are sunk costs ignored?

They have already been spent, and the decision cannot change them. Only future cash flows that differ according to the decision are relevant.

What does a profitability index of 1.14 mean?

Each rupee invested brings back ₹1.14 in present value terms, so the project creates value. The index is useful when capital is limited.
